transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been feeling really weighed down by this thought that I’ve messed things up for my family. We took on this mortgage, and I keep feeling like that was on me, like I pushed us into something too big, and now every little thing feels like proof that I’m not handling life the way I’m supposed to.

Like at work, I’m a waiter, and if I forget something small or a customer looks annoyed, I don’t just think, “Okay, that was a mistake.” I go straight to, “Of course, you’re useless, you can’t even do this right.” And then it sort of spirals into feeling like I deserve whatever bad thing happens because I brought it on myself. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but it feels very real in the moment, and it’s been hard to shake.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge, even when there's no obvious reason to feel that way?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I do get tense sometimes, but I usually connect it to something—like work, money, the house, whether I’ve disappointed someone. I don’t know if I’d say it comes out of nowhere for no reason.

It’s more like my mind starts chewing on something and then my body follows along, if that makes sense. But just sitting there feeling nervous with no obvious reason… I haven’t really noticed that as its own thing. Maybe I’m not paying attention to it the right way, though.
Have you been feeling sad most of the time lately?

Yeah… most days, I think so. It’s not always like I’m openly crying or anything obvious like that. It’s more this heavy, empty feeling in my chest that just kind of sits there.

I’ll be at work carrying plates, smiling at customers, saying the usual things because that’s what you’re supposed to do, and from the outside I probably look normal enough. But inside it feels like I’m just moving through the day without really feeling anything good. Like I’m performing being okay, if that makes sense. Some moments are lighter than others, but lately that sadness or emptiness is there a lot of the time.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, empty feeling inside?

It’s been… a while. If I try to put an actual time on it, I’d say about a year and a couple months now. Maybe around fourteen months.

It hasn’t been exactly the same every single day, like some days I can distract myself or I get through work and it’s not as loud, but the depressed feeling and the guilt have been around for that long overall. It’s not like it just started last week or even a few months ago. It’s been kind of sitting there in the background for more than a year.
Have you had any periods over the last 14 months where you felt completely back to normal, without any of these depressed feelings or guilt?

No… not completely back to normal, I don’t think. There have been better stretches, like days where I’m more distracted or work keeps me busy enough that I’m not sitting with it the whole time. And sometimes I can laugh at something or have a decent few hours, so it’s not like every single minute has been the exact same.

But if you mean, like, a real period where the depressed feeling and the guilt were just gone and I felt like myself again… no, I can’t really say that happened. Over this whole roughly year and two months, it’s been there in some form. Maybe quieter sometimes, more in the background, but not absent.
Have you experienced any other periods like this in your life before the last fourteen months?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I’ve definitely had rough times before, like anyone has, where I was down for a while or felt stressed or disappointed with myself. But if you mean something like this same kind of ongoing heaviness that just keeps hanging around day after day for months and months… I don’t know that I can point to another time like that clearly.

It’s hard because when I look back, my memory kind of blurs things together. I can remember being unhappy during certain periods, but I don’t know if it was this persistent, or if it lifted more normally back then. This last year or so feels different mostly because of how long it’s been sitting there without really going away.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep over the last fourteen months?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, honestly. I mean, I sleep, but I haven’t been keeping track of it or anything, so it’s hard for me to say whether it’s changed in a clear way over the whole fourteen months.

Some nights feel normal enough, and other nights I might stay up too late just because I’m thinking or I don’t feel ready to go to bed, but I don’t know if that’s really a sleep problem or just… life, you know? I haven’t noticed one big pattern that I could point to, like “this started then” or “it’s been this many hours every night.” I guess I’d say I’m not sure I’ve noticed a definite change.
Have you noticed any decrease in the pleasure you get from activities you used to enjoy?

I don’t know if I’d say there’s been a clear decrease, exactly. I mean… I still enjoy some things when I actually do them. Like if I’m watching something funny, or having a decent conversation, or eating something I like, I can still feel that it’s good. It’s not like everything went completely flat or nothing ever feels nice.

But I guess sometimes I don’t go looking for enjoyable things as much, if that makes sense. Like I might not make plans or I might put things off, but I don’t know if that’s because I’m enjoying them less or just because I’m tired of thinking about everything. So… I’m not totally sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a big obvious loss of pleasure, though.
Are these feelings of sadness and heaviness something you experience for most of the day, or are they more intermittent?

It’s more like… most of the day, most days, I think. Not every single second, because if I’m busy at work or someone’s talking to me, I can sort of get pulled into what I’m doing. But underneath it, there’s this heaviness that’s just kind of there.

It’s hard to describe without sounding dramatic, but it feels like this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like I’m going through the motions a lot of the time. At the restaurant, I’ll be carrying plates, smiling at people, saying the usual things, trying to be polite and normal because that’s what I’m supposed to do. And from the outside I probably look fine enough. But inside it doesn’t feel connected to anything good. It’s like I’m acting the part of myself.

So I guess it can fade into the background for a bit, but I wouldn’t call it just coming and going. It’s more like it’s sitting there most of the day, and I notice it whenever things get quiet or I’m not distracted.
Do you find that your feelings of sadness and heaviness change with the seasons?

I don’t think it really changes with the seasons, not in a way I’ve noticed. Like, I can’t say winter makes it this way or summer fixes it or anything like that.

It’s more just… most days, regardless of what it’s like outside, there’s this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I’ll be at work carrying plates, smiling at people, saying “sure, no problem,” doing all the normal waiter stuff because that’s what I’m supposed to do. And I can do it, I guess. But inside it doesn’t feel like I’m actually feeling anything good from it. It’s more like I’m going through the motions and trying to look normal.

So, no, I wouldn’t really connect it to the seasons. It feels more constant than that.
Do you find that you no longer enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable?

I’m not sure I’d put it that strongly, like “no longer enjoy.” I don’t think it’s completely gone. If I actually sit down and do something I used to like, sometimes I can still get something out of it. It might take me a while to get into it, or I might not feel motivated to start, but once I’m there, it’s not like I feel absolutely nothing.

I guess that’s where I get a little confused with the question, because I don’t always seek things out the way I used to, but I don’t know if that means I don’t enjoy them anymore. It’s more like everything feels like effort first, and the enjoyment part is less obvious until I’m already doing it. So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed that I no longer enjoy pleasurable things. It’s not that clear-cut for me.
Have your feelings of sadness and heaviness stayed about the same over the last fourteen months, or have they gotten better or worse at any point?

It’s been… mostly the same, I think. I mean, there are better hours or worse hours, depending on what I’m doing or how busy I am, but the overall feeling hasn’t really lifted in any lasting way.

Most days there’s still that heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It’s like I’ll be at work carrying plates, smiling at tables, saying the right things because that’s what I’m supposed to do, and I can get through it. I can look normal enough, I guess. But it doesn’t feel like I’m doing it because I feel good or connected to anything. It’s more like I’m just moving through the motions.

So if you mean over time, like whether there was a stretch where it clearly got better or worse, I don’t know that I’d say that. It’s more like it’s been sitting there in the background most days, and sometimes I’m distracted from it, but when things quiet down, it’s still there.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite over the last fourteen months?

Yeah… my appetite’s been kind of inconsistent, I guess. Not like one simple direction, like “I stopped eating” or “I’m eating more all the time.” It’s more all over the place.

Some weeks at work, they’ll put out staff meal and I’ll barely touch it. I’ll look at it and know I should eat because I’ve been on my feet, but it just feels like too much effort or I don’t really want anything. Then other nights I get home and it’s the opposite — I’ll just stand in the kitchen and eat whatever’s there, not even because I’m hungry exactly, more like I’m trying to feel settled or filled up somehow.

So yeah, it’s changed in that way. It hasn’t been steady. It sort of swings back and forth.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you didn't feel this heavy, empty feeling and weren't experiencing these depressive thoughts?

No… I don’t think so. Not a full two months.

I’ve had better days, or maybe a week here and there where it wasn’t right in my face all the time, but when I look back on it, the heavy, empty feeling and the guilty kind of thoughts have been pretty much there for about a year and two months. Like, they shift around in intensity, and sometimes I’m distracted enough that I can function and not be thinking about it every second, but I wouldn’t say there was a whole stretch of two months where it was just gone.

If anything, it’s more like I got used to carrying it around, so some days I notice it less. But it’s still been there through this whole period.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level over the last fourteen months?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that one. I don’t know that I’ve noticed a clear change, like I could say, “Oh, my energy dropped in this month,” or “then it came back.” It’s more… day to day, I guess.

With my job, sometimes I’m on my feet for a whole shift and I can still get through it because I have to. I’ll be tired afterward, but that also feels kind of normal for waiting tables, so it’s hard for me to separate what’s just physical tiredness from something else. Some days I feel more drained than others, but I don’t know if I’d call it a big change over the whole fourteen months.

So… I guess I haven’t noticed a really obvious shift in energy, not in the way I noticed the heaviness being there. It’s harder for me to pin down.
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt this depressed, or is this the first time you've experienced it for such a long duration?

This is the first time it’s lasted this long, I think. I mean, I’ve felt down before in my life, sure, and I’ve had stretches where I felt guilty or heavy about things, but not like this… not where it just sort of stayed around and became the background of everything.

This time it’s been about a year and two months, more or less, that those depressed and guilty periods have been there. It’s not always the exact same every day — some days it’s louder, some days I can kind of push through and not focus on it as much — but it hasn’t really let up for any long stretch. So yeah, in terms of it going on this long, this feels like the first time.
Have you experienced any other episodes of depression like this before in your life?

I don’t think so, no… not like this.

I’ve had times before where I was sad or felt bad about myself, or where things felt harder than usual, but I wouldn’t call them the same as this. They didn’t stretch on and on in the same way, where it feels like it becomes part of the background every day. Before, it was more like I could connect it to something or it would pass after a while, even if it felt awful at the time.

This one feels different mostly because of how long it’s been hanging around. I keep trying to look back and compare it to other times, but I don’t really remember another episode that had this same weight to it or lasted anywhere close to this long. So I guess my answer is… no, not really. Not another one like this.
Have you had any other episodes of feeling this depressed before this one started?

I don’t think I’ve had another one like this before, not really. I mean, I’ve had periods where I felt low or guilty about things, but this one is the one that’s been going on and on.

It’s been about a year and two months now where those depressed, guilty periods have been present during this whole stretch. Not every single minute in the exact same way, but it keeps coming back and staying around enough that it feels like it’s been part of my life for that whole time. Before this started, I can’t really point to another episode that lasted like that.
Have you had more than one episode of depression in your lifetime?

I’m not sure I’d count it as more than one, honestly. I mean, I’ve definitely had times in my life where I felt really down or ashamed or like I wasn’t doing well, but when you say “episode of depression,” I think of something more solid than just a rough patch, and I don’t know that I’ve had that more than once.

This current one is the one that stands out to me. Before that, there were bad periods, but they felt more like they came and went, or were tied to whatever was happening at the time. I wouldn’t want to say yes and make it sound like I’ve had repeated full episodes, because I don’t really think that’s accurate. So… no, I don’t think more than one. At least not that I can clearly identify.
Have you had any other episodes of depression that lasted for two weeks or more before this current one started?

I don’t think so… not that I can clearly remember.

Two weeks is a little tricky because, looking back, there were definitely stretches where I’d say I was unhappy or stressed or felt down for a while, and maybe if I looked at a calendar I could find times that were close to that. But in terms of something I’d recognize as depression lasting two weeks or more, before this current thing started, I don’t really have one I can point to and say, yes, that was definitely an episode.

It’s more like before this, things would dip and then come back up, or it felt connected to some situation and eventually shifted. This current one is the one that feels different and more continuous. So I’d say no, not really—at least not one that I’m aware of or that stands out that way.

target_item.manifestation: The depressed, guilty periods have been present for about 1 year and 2 months of this whole time.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration and continuity of depressive symptoms, specifically whether there was a two-month period without the heavy, empty feeling or depressive thoughts.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. Not a full two months.

I’ve had better days, or maybe a week here and there where it wasn’t right in my face all the time, but when I look back on it, the heavy, empty feeling and the guilty kind of thoughts have been pretty much there for about a year and two months. Like, they shift around in intensity, and sometimes I’m distracted enough that I can function and not be thinking about it every second, but I wouldn’t say there was a whole stretch of two months where it was just gone.

If anything, it’s more like I got used to carrying it around, so some days I notice it less. But it’s still been there through this whole period.

doctor.intent: Determine if there are any significant changes in energy levels
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your energy level over the last fourteen months?

target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about changes in energy level or fatigue, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific fatigue/loss-of-energy item.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how to answer that one. I don’t know that I’ve noticed a clear change, like I could say, “Oh, my energy dropped in this month,” or “then it came back.” It’s more… day to day, I guess.

With my job, sometimes I’m on my feet for a whole shift and I can still get through it because I have to. I’ll be tired afterward, but that also feels kind of normal for waiting tables, so it’s hard for me to separate what’s just physical tiredness from something else. Some days I feel more drained than others, but I don’t know if I’d call it a big change over the whole fourteen months.

So… I guess I haven’t noticed a really obvious shift in energy, not in the way I noticed the heaviness being there. It’s harder for me to pin down.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's depressive episode is persistent or recurrent
doctor.question: Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt this depressed, or is this the first time you've experienced it for such a long duration?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depressed, guilty periods have been present for about 1 year and 2 months of this whole time.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how long this depressed period has lasted and whether there have been other similar depressive periods; the closest profile item is the duration of the current depressive episode.

patient.answer:
This is the first time it’s lasted this long, I think. I mean, I’ve felt down before in my life, sure, and I’ve had stretches where I felt guilty or heavy about things, but not like this… not where it just sort of stayed around and became the background of everything.

This time it’s been about a year and two months, more or less, that those depressed and guilty periods have been there. It’s not always the exact same every day — some days it’s louder, some days I can kind of push through and not focus on it as much — but it hasn’t really let up for any long stretch. So yeah, in terms of it going on this long, this feels like the first time.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's depressive episode is recurrent
doctor.question: Have you experienced any other episodes of depression like this before in your life?

target_item.reason: The question asks about prior lifetime episodes of depression like the current one, but the symptom profile only describes the current depressive episode and its duration, not past depressive episode history.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so, no… not like this.

I’ve had times before where I was sad or felt bad about myself, or where things felt harder than usual, but I wouldn’t call them the same as this. They didn’t stretch on and on in the same way, where it feels like it becomes part of the background every day. Before, it was more like I could connect it to something or it would pass after a while, even if it felt awful at the time.

This one feels different mostly because of how long it’s been hanging around. I keep trying to look back and compare it to other times, but I don’t really remember another episode that had this same weight to it or lasted anywhere close to this long. So I guess my answer is… no, not really. Not another one like this.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's depressive episode is recurrent
doctor.question: Have you had any other episodes of feeling this depressed before this one started?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depressed, guilty periods have been present for about 1 year and 2 months of this whole time.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether there were prior episodes of depression before the current one, which relates most directly to the timing and course of the depressive episode.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I’ve had another one like this before, not really. I mean, I’ve had periods where I felt low or guilty about things, but this one is the one that’s been going on and on.

It’s been about a year and two months now where those depressed, guilty periods have been present during this whole stretch. Not every single minute in the exact same way, but it keeps coming back and staying around enough that it feels like it’s been part of my life for that whole time. Before this started, I can’t really point to another episode that lasted like that.

doctor.intent: determine if this is a single episode of depression or recurrent episodes
doctor.question: Have you had more than one episode of depression in your lifetime?

target_item.reason: The question asks about the lifetime number of depressive episodes, but the symptom profile only covers current depressive symptoms and their duration, not whether there have been multiple lifetime episodes.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d count it as more than one, honestly. I mean, I’ve definitely had times in my life where I felt really down or ashamed or like I wasn’t doing well, but when you say “episode of depression,” I think of something more solid than just a rough patch, and I don’t know that I’ve had that more than once.

This current one is the one that stands out to me. Before that, there were bad periods, but they felt more like they came and went, or were tied to whatever was happening at the time. I wouldn’t want to say yes and make it sound like I’ve had repeated full episodes, because I don’t really think that’s accurate. So… no, I don’t think more than one. At least not that I can clearly identify.

doctor.intent: Determine if this is a single episode of depression or recurrent episodes
doctor.question: Have you had any other episodes of depression that lasted for two weeks or more before this current one started?

target_item.reason: The question asks about past depressive episodes lasting two weeks or more before the current one, but the provided symptom profile only covers the current depressive symptoms and their duration, not prior depressive episode history.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not that I can clearly remember.

Two weeks is a little tricky because, looking back, there were definitely stretches where I’d say I was unhappy or stressed or felt down for a while, and maybe if I looked at a calendar I could find times that were close to that. But in terms of something I’d recognize as depression lasting two weeks or more, before this current thing started, I don’t really have one I can point to and say, yes, that was definitely an episode.

It’s more like before this, things would dip and then come back up, or it felt connected to some situation and eventually shifted. This current one is the one that feels different and more continuous. So I’d say no, not really—at least not one that I’m aware of or that stands out that way.
